Get the essential key items in GTA 6 that will make you a more effective criminal

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you've been having a look around in the Progress section of the GTA 6 Index, you've most likely spotted the Equipment tab. There are 12 unique pieces of Equipment in GTA 6, all of it essential for finding new ways to explore the map and generally being a better criminal.

While all of the GTA 6 Equipment unlocks progressively throughout the main GTA 6 missions list, if you're feeling a little impatient I'm here to help you understand what's coming later down the line. I'm going to detail what each piece of equipment does in GTA 6, how it can be used, and where it can be unlocked.

The Binoculars in GTA 6 can be used to scope out enemy targets, mark enemies on the map, identify animals from afar, and even let you participate in a little bird watching (there are 60 of them in total across Leonida). The Binoculars can be equipped at all times from your loadout by holding L1/LB and selecting them from there.

The Flashlight in GTA 6 can be used to help bring a little light to dark buildings and the world itself at night. Admittedly, it's a little cumbersome, so consider going to an Ammu-Nation and fitting a torch to one of your weapons. If you don't want to go that route, then open your loadout with L1/LB, scrolls to where the binoculars are; use left and right on the D-pad on the equipment slot to select the flashlight.

Stash bags are essential in GTA 6, letting Jason and Lucia get out from banks and other robbery targets with more than $20,000 in Pocket Cash. Each character can hold up-to two duffel bags at any one time, and any narcotics, jewellery, or marked bills you pick up will automatically be thrown inside. Stash bags have different capacities, which are determined depending on the size of the building you're robbing.

As soon as you're able to free-roam the world in the Gear Up mission, you're free to purchase a pair of headphones. This is entirely optional, but buying headphones in GTA 6 will let you listen to music and podcasts outside of a vehicle. Purchase headphones and earbuds at any electronics store in the world for both Jason and Lucia – just beware: these can be knocked off your head and become lost.

Have you noticed any sealed wooden crates in your travels across Leonida? Well, more often than not they can actually be broken into – often containing ammunition, weapons, collectibles, and more. You'll get the Pry Bar added to your loadout during Chapter 3, where it will equip automatically as soon as Jason or Lucia approach an openable wooden box.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

The Gear Up mission in Chapter 1 is your first opportunity to purchase a mask. These are used to help conceal Jason and Lucia's identities during robberies. While you will unlock a couple throughout the story, you can buy them early or accrue more of them in different styles. You can learn how to buy a mask here, which also has tips on how to equip and fashion them in different ways.

The Metal Detector is a piece of equipment that you'll need if you want to participate in a side-activity called Underwater Discoveries. Thankfully, this isn't something that you need to purchase. Instead, it'll become a part of your life after you begin doing work for Kenton as part of the main story, and can later be equipped from owned or borrowed boats before you head underwater.

The Slim Jim is a vital piece of equipment. Up until the Moses mission in Chapter 2, the only way you could steal a car was by smashing in its window – a noisy activity which draws attention. The vehicle fence will give you this item for free, allowing you to silently break into cars. It equips automatically whenever you approach a relevant car, and you can learn more about how to use a Slim Jim here.

The Snap Gun isn't available from the beginning of the game, but is well worth pushing into Chapter 3 for. During the Boobie's Time mission, you'll be introduced to a jewellery fence named Yasmani. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that you can help him with a few robberies. Once you've learned how to get the Snap Gun in GTA 6, you'll be able to open locked doors without setting off alarms.

Early on into Chapter 3, you'll have the option to go and meet Brian and Lori. You'll later find yourself down at the docklands, to break into yellow Scoop containers. From that point on, the equipment is yours to keep. You can learn more about how to use the Cut-Off Tool in GTA 6 here, and also find more information on what it can be used to break into later on.

You'll want to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 as fast as you can. This handy phone application is what you'll use to break into more modern vehicles, keyless cars that aren't going to be stolen through mere hotwiring alone. It takes a little while to reach the relevant mission in Chapter 3, but I would recommend you push through the story to get here if you want more to do in the world.

Have you tried robbing any Marked Bills without a Dye Pack Jammer? If yes, you've probably had to go home to change your clothes and have a shower to get the pink dye off. The Dye Pack Jammer automatically disables explosive dye packs which are hidden in Marked Bills, which is why learning how to get the Dye Pack Jammer in GTA 6 is essential if you want to rob a bank or payday loans store.

#3731. World of Warcraft: Forever has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years, says Blizzard

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

"Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!"

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the new edition.

Since it launched on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard said WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most new players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players.

#3730. Alt Video is a digital, faux Blockbuster video store that you can fill with movies from your Letterboxd watchlist and Plex server

And you can even watch those movies in-game

Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.

This is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own. With Alt Video, you do things slightly differently just because of the focus on a different format. So, say you have a Letterboxd account. After exporting some data from your account, you can bring that into Alt Video, and this fake video store will then get filled up with shelves of DVD cases of all the films you've watched.

Alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store. What's more interesting here is that there's a cinema room in the store that lets you watch films on your Plex server, and it's possible to invite your Steam friends to watch along with you. There's even a few other rooms, like a '90s bedroom or family room for more of a CRT kinda vibe. It's cute! If you like you can even manually add any DVDs or Blu-rays you own to appear on all the shelves too.

There's a lot of other nice touches too. In the case of your Letterboxd data, your ratings even show up on the back of the boxes. It's not just relegated to films either, you can put in shows or even your games. The whole thing can be played in VR if you really want that immersive feel. There's a store clerk who can give you some recommendations if you're not sure what to watch. And there's even a day and night system, weather, and seasonal shopfront facelifts.

Alt Video is currently slated for release next week on November 24th, and it'll be doing so in early access. Worth noting that for now the focus is on the browsing, but features involving serving customers and running the store are on the way. You can wishlist it on Steam right here.

There are a lot of new Disney movies that have come out this year, but few are as exciting as Walt Disney Animation’s Hexed. It’s also especially exciting when a release like this means a new character has arrived at Disney Parks. So, that got me wondering: could the new magic-focused movie find a home at one of the resorts permanently? With that in mind, I had to field some early ideas from the movie’s directors when CinemaBlend visited Disney's studio in Burbank, California.

Before we get to that, it should be noted that Billie from Hexed is now meeting guests at Disneyland starting today, and she will be at Hollywood Studios at Walt Disney World starting Wednesday. Check out a first look at how she looks as a Disney Parks character:

A post shared by Disney Parks (@disneyparks)

She looks so good! Disney Parks really got all the details right, making it look like she jumped right out of the new movie. It hasn’t been revealed yet where Billie will be stationed, but I think she would fit right into the upcoming Villains Land. She’s not a villain herself, but she’s from a world of witches, and the vibes just seem to fit. When I shared this idea with the directors of Hexed, one half of the team, Jason Hand, said this:

Villain Land? What about a whole entire land just for Hexe?

OK, now we’re talking! The Hexed trailer shows off a gorgeous new land called Hexe where all witches live. In the new animated movie, Billie opens a secret portal to Hexe after accidentally taking off a bracelet she’s worn all her life that has been concealing her powers. Hexe is a whimsical, beautiful land full of lush forests and magic (of course). Just take a look:

Gorgeous, right? I know I’d especially love to see a recreation of the home of Beef Roger, who is a three-eyed cat who lives on the outskirts of Hexe. Here it is:

I know, I know, perhaps it’s a little too soon to dream up Disney Parks concepts for the movie. It’s not even out yet. But Hexed is getting a ton of positive early reactions for being “unexpected”, and as someone who’s seen the latest from Walt Disney Animation, the studio has definitely created the kind of world I want to visit in real life. Hence, my enthusiasm.

I love how big Jason Hand was thinking regarding how Hexed could fit into Disney Parks, because why not? There’s already a ton of really exciting upcoming Disney attractions on the way, from Monstropolis to Piston Peak; who’s to say Hexed couldn’t become the next. When you check out Hexed, in theaters November 25, you can imagine how you’d like to see it show up in Disney Parks.

#3728. Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

From Ezio Auditore to 17th century witch hunts, Patrice Désilets talks 1666 Amsterdam's devilish origins, everchanging mechanics, and the process of making a game with a community

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Patrice Désilets is known as the father of Assassin's Creed, but his newest baby is his entire world. Panache Digital Games' 1666 Amsterdam finally launched into Early Access in August 2026, the spoils of a hard-won IP battle between Désilets and former employer Ubisoft after he left the studio for the last time in 2013. The timing of its launch seems eerily prescient now that Assassin's Creed Codename Hexe – rumored to be Ubisoft's own witch trials-themed action-adventure – has been reportedly delayed by a year. Having launched into Early Access before Hexe was given a proper reveal, 1666 Amsterdam feels like a bold statement, a flag on the moon of this particular space race: We were here first.

Speaking to me at Gamescom, Xbox controller in-hand to show off the Early Access build that had launched that same week, Désilets reflected on the long road to getting Noa's story into players' hands – even if he still expects it to undergo many more changes on the journey to v1.0.

We're sharing this full interview transcript exclusively with our members, offering an extra peek into Patrice's approach to development. If you'd like to read the whole thing, you can do so simply by signing in, or by registering for free - just enter your email address below.

GamesRadar+: Why don't we first talk about how it feels now to have the game in Early Access after so many years of being in your brain? It must be quite mind-boggling.

Patrice Désilets: It's a mixed thing because it's like, "Oh! It's up there!" [gesturing to the game displayed on the TV]. But on Monday we have to continue working on it. But it's great. At the end there's always some doubts – am I crazy for wanting to do this for 15 years? Should I just move on? But it's like no, no, no! Because it's a good thing that I stuck with it even though it changed so much somehow in those 16 years.

If you think about it, it was my first game right after Assassin's Creed, right? So I was really tainted by Ezio and Altair and the ruleset that we'd built over the years. So at first, [1666 Amsterdam] was all about the devil. Like, you played the devil. And I went back to it in 2020, and was like, "I don't want to talk about that anymore. Back to square one again." [I asked myself] What would be the character that represented that devilish side of the world? Like, oh, witches! And I'm not 'the witch guy' at first, right? But I was like, oh, it's perfect. Let's do with witches what I did with Assassins, and let's create an open world and a badass witch using the broom and not the old lady inside a little hut in the woods. So that's how it all started, and now it's out there and people are giving us feedback. The great part is that our goal now is actually to listen and make it better with them.

With magical combat, city sleuthing, and physical roguelike charms, I can't wait for 1666 Amsterdam

GR+: You mentioned at the hands-on preview that your whole dream behind making Panache was to eventually make a game with the community. So how has the feedback been so far? Like, has it made you think, "okay, now I know what I want to do," even while you're here at Gamescom?

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

PD: Just like you didn't have a chance to play it yet, I didn't have a chance to actually look at the feedback yet because I'm here talking with people. What I just learned is that my team is excited in Montreal. They're really already in the [mindset of] "okay, yes, there's this and that we can change." They have ideas. And that's kind of how we work – we work in an iterative process, so we listen to the game, listen to ourselves. So it's not about me and my design, saying, "This is what I want, let's do this!"

There's a lot of things that we tried and ultimately went like, "Ah, you know what, guys, it doesn't work." Like for a while, you didn't play as a cat. Could you imagine? You could possess cats, for a long period of time [in development]. But I was afraid to have a witch and a cat. I was afraid of people going "oh, he's doing cliché stuff there." But like, man, it's a witch! And then what if the cat is the guy from 1999? Because he [the character of Aaron] was just a spectral [humanoid] figure for a long period of time, there to possess people. But what if he's possessing a cat in 1666? And then you'll have the two worlds of 1999 and 1666, two halves woven together all the time, and the relationship between the two characters will make it a whole? And but that's not me being so fucking genius with that, ordering people about. That's not at all how I work. So that's why now [in Early Access], it's just more people telling us, "This is good, this is not that good." We're used to it.

GR+: Talking of changes, I remember last time you mentioned that you lose all Noa's abilities when you die, and that you need to go back and find them all over again in the open world. But it's different now in Early Access?

PD: Yes, because we are listening! We did some playtests and people were like, "Are you fucking crazy? I spent two hours finding all of this, and you removed them all." So what we do now is that for every coffer and curiosity cabinet you find, you get a new type of ability. Once you find them, you're fine. But when you fail, you just redo a big lottery, so you'll have new abilities and some of them will be the same. But you don't have to find them all over again. So you may approach the mission differently this time because you don't have some of the abilities you had. It messes a bit with your brain, like, "Okay, I had the Warp mechanic. I was good in fights and now I'm less physically powerful, but I'm stronger in Compulsion." So you have to approach the mission differently. And when you finish an Esbat – when you finish like a full moon cycle – then you can lock one or two abilities forever.

GR+: So it really does sound like everything is open to – well, not suggestion, but would you say everything is open to discussion when it comes to the making of the game and how you take on community feedback?

PD: [laughs] Well, eventually there's a limit to the listening! If you don't want a cat but a different animal instead, like, no. You're having a cat. The narrative is our thing. The story – we're writing it, and it'll be a surprise for players. But there's always going to be something cool mechanics-wise that we were never aware of, that the community will come up with.

It's the beauty of making games now. We're in Early Access. Okay, it's not finished, we know. So it's part of the process. But real data comes back, not wishful thinking, and we can actually adjust for real, a little ease of play. Our goal is that we have our backlog of ideas and things we want to do. If the community has the same idea and it aligns, this is priority number one [to implement]. Other than that: we have a plan.

#3726. Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises."

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever."

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

Ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its new operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft says the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active users over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft announced in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

Jason and Cal do their best to redecorate the bach' pad but c'mon boys, a TV in front of a giant glass door? We can do better.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals doing crimes. Car crimes, gun crimes, drug crimes, and first degree decorating crimes. Early in the game, Jason's buddy Cal convinces him that he's got to turn his r/malelivingspace shack into a place he can bring his girl Lucia without feeling like she's still stuck in a jail cell. Cal is right, but his decorating decisions should be illegal.

This is how Jason's living room looks at the beginning of the game while he's still flying solo. Not great, Jason. If I've learned anything from lurking in interior decorating communities online it's that furniture should never be touching your walls, no matter how small the room is, and that nobody's TV is ever at the right height.

Cal hassles Jason into moving some things around and, while I love his motivation, he makes everything worse. What they wind up with is this: couch blocking prime navigation space and the TV sitting in front of the sliding glass door. Look, I know the point is that Cal is an incompetent dork. He's slugging beers and insisting they make the room feng shui. I can't forgive him for this one though.

Cal does get one thing right here: using the couch and arm chair to create a space that feels like a living room within the open area. Once Lucia moves in she and Jason continue making the waterfront shack more homey. They get a rug in the living room, a classic choice to finish tying that space into a room. Lucia brings home a coffee table to assemble (cute domestic conversation ensues). The dining table gets centered properly in its corner.

But that damn TV stays parked in front of the glass door. It's criminal! There would be so much glare on that screen from the east and west facing windows and light all day long drowning it out from behind that north facing glass door. My sad, myopic eyes are tearing up just thinking about squinting at it.

So I took Jason's conundrum to one of the interior decorating communities on Reddit to ask for some group workshopping. They immediately grasped the unforgivable TV placement and the inherent issue with the number of windows in this place. Almost no wall is safe here.

One suggestion was to keep those window blinds in the living room down and place the TV stand in front of it. Makes sense to me—Jason wouldn't be losing much light with all the other windows in here. Another more minor fix was to just put the TV at a 45 degree angle in its corner so it's less directly in front of the glass door, though I don't think that solves the glare problems.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The more popular suggestion (and my favorite) was to swap the dining and living room. The TV can sit on the rear wall, slightly tucked away with the blinds pulled down, while the dining table gets easier access from the kitchen and doesn't suffer for being lit from all sides.

Alas, I have it on good authority that the TV never manages to move from where Cal stuck it. I can forgive drug smuggling, but I draw the line at suboptimal viewing angles. Ah well, perhaps Jason and Lucia have a better floor plan to work with in the next place they move to as their criminal exploits grow.

#3724. Blizzard wants to "get rid" of best-in-slot items in World of Warcraft: Forever by introducing situationally strong gear

"BIS is not a good thing for a game that's supposed to be about role-playing."

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different."

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list."

Moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

It's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ever since Tony premiered on the 2026 movie schedule, I’ve been looking forward to rewatching it with an HBO Max subscription. That’s because it’s such a lovely and unexpectedly heartwarming film about Anthony Bourdain’s cooking origins, and I found myself wanting to hang out in Provincetown again. However, while I did that, I also learned that the director Matt Johnson and star Dominic Sessa don’t exactly feel the same way about the film, as they described making it as “being stabbed in the stomach.”

When CinemaBlend’s Hannah Saulic sat down to chat with the cast and director of the critically acclaimed Tony, she told them she loved the movie and described it as a “warm hug.” Matt Johnson went on to say he’s actually heard this sentiment from “so many people.” And Stavros Halkias, who plays Dimitri in the movie, noted that “it is sentimental.”

I couldn’t agree more. The found family element of this film is honestly quite wholesome (despite the chaos). Along with that, hanging out with Tony as he figures out his life and falls in love with cooking is a really good time. Plus, there are parts of Tony that genuinely make me emotional. So, yes, in many ways, the movie is heartwarming, because he finds his people and his calling, and who wouldn’t want to spend time watching him do that?

However, making this movie was a totally different story. Making that point very clear, Dominic Sessa, who plays Tony, and Johnson, who directed it, had this to say:

Well, I can’t say I blame Sessa, specifically, for having this reaction. I mean, the best gag in Tony is the one where he gets splashed in the face with water over and over again. He told us that filming those scenes “sucked,” and Johnson described Sessa’s experience with this gag as “a kind of prison torture."

So, I can see why they’d also note that filming the movie didn’t feel like a hug, and in a way felt like getting “stabbed in the stomach.”

However, again, that’s not how it reads on screen. As a movie, Tony is wonderful and not a torturous watch at all. To that point, Stavros Halkias jumped into the conversation to say:

Well, loukoumades are Greek donuts with honey, and they look delectable. And like Halkias pointed out, Tony is like a warm treat for viewers. Between Tony learning how to cook with Antonio Banderas’ Ciro, his realization that this is what he wanted to do with his life, and that Eric Ripert cameo at the end of the movie that comes with the first time Tony refers to himself as Anthony, it’s hard not to feel heartwarming energy radiating off this A24 flick.

However, when you rewatch it and feel that way, just make sure to remember and appreciate the fact that it was not that warm and cozy to make.

#3722. GTA 6 Includes Compelling Evidence That It’s Set In The Same Universe As Red Dead Redemption

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Red Dead Redemption 2

Grand Theft Auto 6 contains a few new interesting pieces of evidence that seem to indicate Rockstar’s popular crime-sim franchise lives in the same universe as its also-popular cowboy series, Red Dead Redemption.

Let’s start with one of the most compelling and obvious connections between GTA 6 and Red Dead: a book you can find in the new game that directly references events from RDR 2. As spotted and shared online by GameRoll, there’s a book players can find early on in Brian’s Marina in GTA 6 that contains many references to both Red Dead Redemption and its prequel, Red Dead Redemption 2. For example, the book mentions a gunslinger players can meet in RDR 2, as well as mentions of locations from those games such as Blackwater and New Austin.

Iâm pleasantly surprised that Rockstar has clearly merged the RDR and GTA universes (I go into an easter egg here so donât read if you donât wanna).

This book in Brianâs Marina has MULTIPLE references to RDR1 and RDR2. It describes the demise of outlaw Flaco Hernandez, who isâ¦ pic.twitter.com/J3xecySXL0

— GameRoll (@GameRoll_) November 20, 2026

A more subtle connection, but one that has some interesting implications, can be randomly spotted on the license plates of some cars in GTA 6. Every so often, you might spot a car with a New Austin license plate. In the world of Red Dead, New Austin is intended to be the game’s version of Texas. Things get a bit weird if you think about all of this too much, as Texas has been mentioned in both franchises before. But then again, GTA V mentions Florida, which has been retconned into Leonida in GTA 6. So this stuff happens sometimes.

A sillier connection to Red Dead can be spotted at a western-themed mini-golf course in GTA 6. If you explore that place, you’ll quickly discover a small dog with a cowboy doll attached to his back. Look closer, and you’ll be able to identify that cowboy as Arthur Morgan.

Found a familiar friend on âhorsebackâ byu/Scholsey01 inGTA6

And speaking of Arthur Morgan, you can actually find what looks a lot like his famous hat in GTA 6, as well. It’s the hat I wear when I go hunting as Jason. Before all this, people spotted connections between RDR2 and GTA 6 in pre-release trailers and screenshots. Some of these connections were also spotted in GTA V, like a president from RDR being featured in artwork.

So does this all mean that GTA 6 is in the same universe as Red Dead Redemption 2? I think it clearly indicates that Rockstar is playing around with that idea. The problem is that if you dig into the lore of both franchises, you’ll find some discrepancies. But Rockstar has shown in the past that it’s willing to simply retcon these kinds of issues without feeling the need to explain anything.

Where where to find and start The Final Flush mission in GTA 6 and earn a stamina upgrade

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Big Flush in GTA 6 is an optional mission, but it's well worth your time for a permanent stamina upgrade. You can start this GTA 6 mission from Chapter 1 onwards, and once it's done it's incredibly useful reward will allow you to do energy-draining activities, like running and swimming, for longer. It's also just a fun side mission to do. After finding an odd poster in a men's bathroom stall, you are enlisted to help oddball Dr. Merle to prove his bizarre conspiracy theory that the government is stealing DNA from poop (which is seemingly based on a real report about Putin) and things only get stranger from there.

To start The Final Flush mission in GTA 6, go to the bathroom block toward the north tip of Corsair Key in Mariana County (just north-east of Key Lento). It should be easy to find as it's the only building in Corsair Key. Enter the men's toilet and you'll see a handmade poster on the wall that says "Stop! Don't Flush.

Scan to learn the truth #NOFLUSHERS" with a QR code attached. Use your WaiNK IT app to scan the code and you'll receive a message from an Automated Machine that tells you to reply "TRUTH" to join the No Flushers movement. Select the "Truth" reply and you'll receive another message telling you that whoever is messaging will be at Frank's Waffles in Vice City. If asked, you need to repeat the code: 00-00-02.

You need to meet the mystery No Flusher at Frank's Waffles in the Tequesta neighborhood of Vice City, in Vice-Dale County. When you enter the waffle house, you'll find a man muttering to himself in one of the booths nearest the toilets. However, he seemingly won't appear if it's not night time, as, when I went during the day, the mission icon had a padlock on it and the man wasn't there.

When you get near the man, he covers up whatever he's working on and tells you that he's holding a royal flush. When he asks do you have a "coda for that?," hold LT/LR while looking at the man to bring up the dialogue menu and select the code option with X/A.

The oddball man is Dr. Merle, who quickly ingests a tracking device and begins waffling (no pun intended) about his conspiracy theory that the poop of Leonida citizens isn't actually going to the sewers but is instead going to a secret government DNA siphoning center. He then goes to the corporate-controlled bathroom to deposit the tracking device into the federally-controlled sewers, so you can track where Leonida's bowel movements go to the source of the whole operation.

Once Dr Merle is done in the bathroom, follow him to his van outside. Follow his verbal directions to follow the tracker and it'll take you to the sewage treatment plant in Hamlet in Vice-Dale County. Follow the waypoint to park the van on the coast then follow Dr Merle on foot to the plant.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

When you reach the plant's fence, Dr. Merle begins unlocking a metal gate so that you can get inside and asks you to keep an eye out. Keep an eye on the road on the other side of the gate as a van will soon approach. If the driver stops and asks what you're doing, the best approach is to use the "Defuse" dialogue option to tell the worker you're simply fixing the gate.

Once you're inside the sewage treatment plant ground, you're tasked with finding the tracker. The best approach is to head toward the area highlighted pink on your GTA 6 map until you see the two works chatting. Approach them and, when asked if you are electricians, use the "Lie" dialogue option to go along with their theory. Go through the open metal gate to the left of the works, then slightly right and you'll see a set of double doors. Enter these doors to enter the facility.

Once you get inside Dr. Merle starts to freak out because the tracking device is apparently below your feet, but there's no obvious way to reach it, so he asks you to find a way down. Go up the metal stairs in this room and you'll find a control panel on the platform above. Select Triangle/Y to interact with the panel.

To open the stairs that lead downstairs, all three lights on the left of the control panel need to be turned to green. So, push the buttons next to the two red lights (the middle and bottom ones), to turn them green, then tilt the main lever on the panel. A secret staircase leading downstairs will then open up where Dr.Merle is sitting.

Go down the stairs and you'll enter a room with a large, mysterious-looking chamber. Determined to prove his DNS-siphoning theory is correct, Dr. Merle gets into the chamber– which soon begins to fill with liquid – and asks you to flush him. Press the red button on the control panel in front of the chamber to do so.

Unfortunately, this puts the water authority on your case. They warn over a loudspeaker that the authorities are on their way and that the chamber is highly toxic, so you absolutely should not step inside it. Step inside the chamber and you'll automatically be flushed. You wake up (somehow) outside Jason's House with a notification telling you your max stamina has increased.

#3719. GTA 6 Has An Impressive Number Of Accessibility Options To Make The Game Less Frustrating

With Grand Theft Auto 6 casting such a wide cultural net, a lot of people of varying levels of video game experience and skill are going to be playing it, some of whom maybe just want to sightsee or experience the story, and they may find a lot of the friction frustrating. Those people might quickly find themselves on the verge of giving up, but luckily, there are accessibility options built into the game that can be used right from the start.

Accessibility options are different from cheats, in that they donât require you to beat the game or perform specific tasks to unlock them. Theyâre there for people who, for whatever reason, arenât able to make progress with the game when playing the game with its standard difficulty, mechanics, or controls. Be warned that messing with some of these options can significantly alter the balance, and thus your enjoyment, of the game.

Also, unlike cheats, accessibility options do not disable trophies or achievements, nor do they prevent you from saving.

At any point in the game, access the pause menu and scroll all the way down to settings.

Select that option and press RB or R1 to reach the Gameplay section.

From here, scroll down to the bottom under âAccessibilityâ to see multiple options. The ones youâll probably most want to pay attention to are those for Simplified Mini Games, Auto Drive, Accessible Combat, and Reduced Vehicle Damage.

Activating “Simplified Mini Games” makes activities like exercising, hotwiring vehicles, and shooting hoops easier and not so reliant on timing or easing off the analog triggers.Â

Auto Drive is an option with its own sub-options, allowing you to have the game drive for you in leisurely situations like getting to a mission or, if you set it to Unrestricted, use it even when youâre being pursued or chasing enemies. The menu warns that the driving AI may still crash into objects or other cars, so itâs not like a free pass for everything to go perfectly.

The two big ones, Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, get their own warnings: The game was not built with this in mind. That means you can turn them on, but things will become significantly easier. If you activate these options without needing them, you may start getting bored playing GTA 6.

Accessible Combat reduces enemy health and also damage done to the player, so youâll hurt them more and they will hurt you less. Reduced Vehicle Damage means your car wonât suffer too much in collisions or shootouts, so a T-Bone or two wonât render your car inoperable.

There are other accessibility options that make certain things like boosting while driving a little friendlier. If you ever have a problem controlling something in the game, itâs worth checking to see if thereâs an accessibility option that would change how it works a little bit. Whatever helps you get through the game!

Chapter 2 of GTA 6 finally gives you full control over both Jason and Lucia, and one of the first missions you'll undertake as a criminal couple involves committing a robbery in one of three locations.

One of your options is Avery Pawn Shop, where you'll be able to make a tidy sum of money if you can smash-and-grab enough loot and, more crucially, find the safe code to crack it open for additional cash and jewellery.The easiest way to do that is to grab the code for the safe, which is thankfully pretty easy to do.

Head inside Avery Pawn with your partner in tow—don't forget to pop on a mask, along with a hat and sunglasses to hide your identity—and begin holding up the store by pulling out your gun with L2 and pointing it at the clerks.

You should be able to threaten one of the staff members with Square and, with the other, the same input should instead change to "Safe Code?" if you look at the bottom-right corner. For me, it was the one standing behind the counter on the left.

The clerk should give up the safe code with little resistance. Once you have it, head behind the counter and into the back room. There'll be another staff member there, but you can point your gun and threaten him as well. Head into the office to the right, input the safe code, and grab your goods.

It looks like, at least where pawn shops are concerned, the code given is random. In my case, the code was 5683, but yours will most likely be different. This method should work for every pawn shop though, not just Avery Pawn!

A blue hippo is making its way back this Thanksgiving

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is hitting a significant milestone this year and will be turning the big 100. To celebrate, they are pulling out all the stops, including adding favorites, both new and old. One returning balloon has fans emotional as the announcement comes after the tragic death of Fiona the Hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden. Now that Macy’s has brought back its blue hippo for the 100th parade, Fiona fans have a request.

The beloved hippo became a global sensation following her premature birth in January 2017, and after receiving round-the-clock care, she began to thrive. She was also the first Nile hippo to be imaged prenatally via ultrasound at the zoo and the first born there in 75 years. However, on November 19, she swallowed a knit hat that was accidentally tossed into her enclosure, and it tragically led to her premature death. The loss hit hard for a lot of fans. One Reddit thread suggests that Macy’s blue hippopotamus “should totally dedicate it to Fiona,” and it has fans responding with comments like:

In addition to the balloon possibly representing Fiona, it also has a long, legendary history. It was first unveiled in 1931, and during that parade, they decided it was a good idea to release giant balloons into New York City. You may be asking yourself, why? I’ll tell you. Each balloon had a price tag, and whoever found a balloon and returned it to the department store would receive that amount as a prize. The blue hippo balloon was never returned, and even after an offer of $100, nobody came forward, leaving the balloon lost to history.

To ring in the parade’s big birthday, they’ve decided to bring back the blue hippo, but this time, it’ll keep its feet tethered to the ground. It will be joining an assortment of new additions, including everything from KPop Demon Hunters to Bluey. There’s something for everyone in the family to enjoy, and if you weren’t already, this year’s celebration could make you become a parade person.

The new balloon is reportedly going to look like a more modern version of the 1931 balloon seen below:

If the blue hippo isn’t enough to sell you on the parade, then maybe some new floats might. We’ll be seeing a variety of newcomers, including "Hogwarts Holiday," which features a Harry Potter-themed float that will celebrate (and promote) the newly rebooted series on HBO kicking off in December. The cool floats and balloons are an opportunity for brands (like Starbucks) to promote themselves with whimsical, colorful, and unique floats or balloons.

Additionally, it will include Tom Jr., which is a new turkey addition to the parade, and Tony Sarg’s Amazing Marionettes, which pays tribute to the original parade puppeteer. There is also a mix of performers to look forward to, including The Voice’s new favorite coach, Queen Latifah.

However, a lot of Fiona fans will be watching to catch sight of the blue hippo and are hopeful it will do her justice with a sweet tribute or at least a special place in the parade.

The big event will hit the 2026 TV schedule on Thanksgiving Day, November 26, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. across time zones. This can be viewed on NBC, Telemundo, or with a Peacock subscription.

#3716. GTA 6 day-one sales are enormous, estimates suggest, making previous $2 billion opening weekend predictions seem conservative

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking company Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

Should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent company Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

#3714. Total War: Warhammer 40,000 breaks the game into star system mini-campaigns, each with their own stories and objectives

"We want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy."

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

The star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do."

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

On the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

"Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that."

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

#3711. UK Prime Minister won't be playing GTA 6, government says, while hailing Rockstar Games a "British success story"

Grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

"Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it."

Downing Street went on to address the issue of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

The leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else."

GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

This state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

#3710. Three Games You Can Play For Free This Weekend On PC

Don’t want to pay $80 for Grand Theft Auto 6? Don’t have a console to play it on? There are alternatives. Here are three games you can play for free on PC this weekned.

Matt Damon was clearly trying to fly under the radar during an August 2026 trip to Disneyland to celebrate his daughter Gia’s 18th birthday. Then he ended up clearly visible in the background of internet comedian and content creator Loryn Powell’s video on Instagram, as her daughter was meeting Goofy for the first time. And the video of the movie star dad smiling as he watched and understood how special the father-daughter moment in front of him was unsurprisingly went vital.

Now Matt Damon himself has commented on the unexpected cameo appearance and the story behind it is even lovelier than I could have imagined. During an interview for The Morning Show in Canada, the star of The Odyssey (one of the biggest box office success stories on the 2026 movie schedule) explained how that sweet moment unfolding in front of him reminded him of all the moments he’d shared with his own daughter at Goofy’s Kitchen in the Disneyland Hotel. You can check out what he had to say about it in this Instagram clip:

A post shared by Loryn Powell (@lorynpowell)

When I first saw the video, I immediately thought, “Now there’s a dad who’s having a flashback of a memory with his own daughter.” So it warmed my heart to hear directly from the Good Will Hunting star that that’s exactly what happened. He, himself, has had that exact moment over the year on annual birthday trips that landed him in that very same spot.

When we think of Matt Damon, we picture the international film star, the public friendship with Ben Affleck, or even the Damon/Kimmel faux feud that started back in the early 2000s. We tend to forget that he has four daughters, which means countless family events, gatherings, birthdays, and shared experiences, and endless memories from when they were children. It was beyond heartwarming to see his reaction in real time as the father and daughter sharing time with Goofy brought him back to his own family.

He got called out on all of this in the interview because the host, Brittnee Blair, had recognized a similar look in her own husband watching their four-year-old daughter, knowing how fast time passes and that those moments will merely be memories. Being the movie star on a press tour that he is, the self-proclaimed “anti-Tom Cruise” also related it back to the movies of Christopher Nolan by saying:

It’s a theme in a lot of Chris’ movies, right? Of a father missing the childhood of their kids. That video, one of my kids sent that to me. We were at Goofy’s Kitchen in Disneyland, and we’ve gone every year for my daughter’s birthday, and she was turning 18… And I had no idea somebody was recording that.

I love when the timing lines up and someone can ask a celebrity to explain the story behind a viral moment, making them more relatable to everyone else. And there’s nothing more human than spending and missing time with our loved ones. I can’t imagine what the family in the video thought when they realized that not only was The Bourne Identity star at Disneyland on the same day, but he was in the background of their video, reacting to that special interaction.

There is no shortage of celebrity sightings at theme parks, from Disney super fan Charlize Theron to John Stamos, Adam Sandler, and so many others. Something like this moment with Matt Damon makes me not only want to keep an even more keen eye out, but also comb through my own videos for anyone making an unexpected cameo appearance in the background. Especially knowing that it could lead to another sweet backstory like this one.

#3708. 8 Amazing Indie Games We Think You Should Go Play

Indie GamesQueen's DomainSonic Pico ParkTanuki: Pon's SummerWell Dweller

I’m seeing reports that some folks have already blazed through GTA 6‘s story, finishing the game roughly 48-ish hours (depending on your time zone) after its release. And of course, there are those gamers who don’t plan on playing the game at all, untouched by the powerfully seductive force of GTA 6 FOMO. Whatever your reason for having a free gaming calendar right now, I’ve come bearing gifts with which you can fill it. I’ve sampled my Kotaku colleagues as well as conducted my own research to assemble a smattering of recently released indie games you can play right now.

Dig Dig Dino was originally released on the Playdate before coming to Steam this week. It’s from the developers of the well-liked western action game Arco, though this time they’ve gone for something much smaller, simpler, and cuter. In Dig Dig Dino you play as an paleontology intern tasked with using your shovel and a growing arsenal of tools to find dinosaur bones. You start with limited stamina, only able to dig so much in a day. But as you chew through layers of dirt and sedimentary rock, you pick up treasure that gets exchanged for cash with which you can buy more more stamina, upgrades for your tools, and new tools like a dog who will sniff out bones for you.

The game sounds almost too simplistic to be any kind of fun, but I found myself spending hours digging, hoping the next run would reveal the final piece to my saurian puzzle. There are different dig sites that require different tools and yield different treasures, but don’t expect to discover the kinds of finds that would excite the dearly departed Dr. Alan Grant. The dinos you discover in this game are weird, and though I’m only a few hours (and a few competed skeletons) in, I suspect there’s a greater mystery about the world to discover as you dig deeper.

Sonic Pico Park may have the blue blur in the name, but itâs developed by the small team at TECOPARK, which created the original Pico Park. The cooperative puzzler lends some Sonic the Hedgehog flair toÂ Pico Park‘s cooperative, ragebait puzzle platforming action. The game is a lot of chaotic fun in which up to eight players will yell at one another, then lock in to solve some difficult challenges. Work on your team-building skills as Sonic, Shadow, and several other characters from across the series. Lone wolves need not apply; youâve gotta play with folks you can still like after youâve been tied to one another and tried to coordinate running through a loop-de-loop. â Kenneth Shepard

Maybe you’re a big fan of Dark Souls, Elden Ring, or even King’s Field. Maybe you’re craving that next Elder Scrolls. Or maybe you’re just not super interested in cars and guns and want something a bit more medieval. Friends, let’s pay a visit to Queen’s Domain, a gorgeous first-person RPG in classic-PlayStation style that combines a very clonky, retro-feeling combat and exploration system with much more smoothness to movement and menuing than the games that inspired it could ever muster. Queen’s Domain has you exploring a mysterious island full of magic and monsters in search of your father. You’re puny and weak when you start, enemies hit hard and sneak up on you, and for the most part the game tells you very little about how to proceed: you just have to experiment and pray. But that’s exactly what some people (like me) want, and the feeling when something finally clicks is exhilirating. I hear there’s a pretty big twist midway through that blows the game wide open, too, though I haven’t experienced it yet for myself. â Rebekah Valentine

Tanuki: Ponâs Summer is one part Tony Hawk, one part mail delivery game, and one part cozy slice-of-life sim. Also, you play as an adorable Tanuki who waddles around the open-world village and forest that make up the game’s map. Iâve had a lot of fun pulling off sick tricks while delivering packages to locals and learning more about them. Sometimes, these moments lead to mini-games in which you help out the villagers with sumo wrestling, running a bar, or chopping down trees. But mostly, you spend a lot of time doing tricks on a BMX bike in a gorgeous little world that Iâve been having a great time poking at between big GTA 6 sessions. â Zack Zwiezen

Wanderburg is a bullet heaven action-roguelike in which you play as a medieval fortress on wheels swerving around the countryside as armies collide and new territories are conquered. Itâs sort of like Vampire Survivors if it starred the castle from Howlâs Moving Castle. Itâs also similar to TerraTech Legion, another vehicular spin on the auto-shooter genre, except with some Age of Empires flavor mixed in. Itâs in Early Access on Steam right now and itâs my go-to run-based arcade shooter for the fall. – Ethan Gach

CRACK is a type of game that’s not usually my bag. Itâs an incremental co-op comedy adventure, not something Iâd usually touch, but my son loves these types of games and so I spent more time with it than I expected to. You live in a mysterious lab with a giant egg in the middle. Your job is to crack pieces of it off and trade them in for money, which you use to get upgrades to get better tools to knock off better chunks of the egg and, well, you can see where this is going. But the egg is alive, and the more you chip away the angrier it gets, eventually causing dangerous outbursts that lead to chaotic mayhem. Thatâs the friendslop part of it. Throw in the mystery of the lab itself, with clear influences from games like Portal, and youâve got a surprisingly clever social twist on making the numbers go up. – Ethan Gach

Well Dweller is the fourth metroidvania by Kyle Thompson, and if you donât know who that is, just think Hollow Knight but shorter and more chill. While seemingly influenced by Team Cherryâs aesthetic sensibility and gameplay formula, Thompson has been refining his own take on the genre for several games now. Plus you know what? Silksong came out over a year ago. We could use a spiritual successor or two, and Well Dweller earns its keep as one of the better ones. You play as a bird with a matchstick that can do all sorts of whimsical things, leading to some satisfying traversal and combat, even if itâs not very deep. For those who want a breezier action metroidvania, thatâs a plus. – Ethan Gach

Have you heard the good word of Dressmaker yet? Dressmaker is about exactly what you think it is: you make dresses. But itâs not just a color-swapping dress-up game. No, youâre doing this stitch-by-stitch. Youâre choosing the fabric, picking out adornments, cutting pieces to patterns along the bias, stitching them together, adding the lace trim, all to customer (or your own) specifications. The ridiculous amount of detail that Dressmaker goes into, coupled with an enormous array of dressmaking options that you unlock as you play, already has made it a beloved favorite this year. And some of the dresses people are making are ridiculous! But whether youâre skilled or just throwing together some cloth, Dressmaker is undeniably delightful. – Rebekah Valentine

#3707. Star Wars: Galactic Racer studio "didn't dream" Biddy Blas would be as popular as he is

"He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly."

Fuse Games, the developer of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has said it "didn't dream" the pod racing game's background character Biddy Blas would become as popular as he has.

Since Galactic Racer's release in October, Blas - who resembles a short, humanoid crocodile (officially a crocin) - has become a viral sensation. The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

"Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!"

Fuse Games shared a comment from Biddy Blas creator and Galactic Racer narrative designer Ren Alex-Rose about the character's success. "We always suspected Biddy Blas would be a popular member of the Galactic League, but we didn't dream of just how popular he'd become," Alex-Rose said.

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole new level.

"It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly."

Blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who said his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer was awarded a full five stars in Eurogamer's review. "Both a surprisingly fun Roguelite campaign and a racing treat for Criterion fans, this is just wonderful stuff," wrote Christian Donlan.

This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

World of Warcraft: Forever's done a lot of things for me over the past couple of weeks—it's given me a deeper appreciation for oldschool MMO quest design, it's wowed me with some genuinely impressive new lighting technology, and it's… ugh, it's made me so friendly.

Mind, I wouldn't say I'm unkind when I play MMOs, but I am a solo player by habit. I'll have a guild, friends I roleplay with, sure. But I'm very rarely striking up conversations with people in-game—all of that typically happens in Discord. And yet, here I am in WoW forever, trying to emphatically start conversations with goddamn everyone I meet.

And it's in part because of how much of a bastard the game is. I don't think Classic is a particularly difficult videogame—I've even gotten my warrior from level 1 to, at the time of writing, 56 as fury, a spec typically considered trash for levelling. And it's been fine, I've just minded my pulls and levelled first aid.

But it is a known fact that vanilla WoW quests are just easier when you group up with people. Part of this is because players are a force multiplier—many classes have group buffs, and not having to worry about health with a healer present means that you can pull swathes of enemies and melt them down easily.

And so I've been doing that. I've been grouping with people, and they've been grouping with me, and… oh, god, we've been talking to each other.

I don't know if I just happen to have a lucky propensity for drawing in nice folks, but my levelling journey has been dappled with some of the chillest people you'll ever meet. People hanging around to help you finish quests they've already completed is so common it's almost standard.

In one instance, a shadow priest carried me through multiple elite quests in Stranglethorn Vale—they needed to do 'em too, sure, but they actively went out of their way to show me where I could get a couple.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

There is a real, tangible sense of camaraderie in the game right now, one that's yet to be grinded to the marrow by the efficiency-laden tasks of Mythic+ or a seasonal system. But it's also one borne of how long everything takes. When you've already spent 10 minutes jogging to a quest, what's another five to help a stranger out?

It is, to put it plainly, the opposite of what I'd expected after years of playing far more modern MMOs. I'm even way ahead of the curve of the general population level-wise, and I'm still meeting these relaxed, generous folks. People who'll offer up scraps of a treasure map that's dropping from the pirates we're grinding for free, rather than being a mercenary about it and selling them on the auction house.

Moreover, it is infectious. I've been handing mana potions to people. I've been sticking around to help out with quests—in a recent Zul'farrak run, a dungeon I was only doing twice because I'd missed that it was required for the Sunken Temple questline, our tank had simply atrocious luck collecting troll tempers for a quest (you need 20 of them, and they don't drop often).

Not just myself, but another player in the same situation all stuck around for about 20 minutes just to help them out. When they thanked us, I, saccharine and glowing with the spirit of a reformed Grinch, said: "No worries, bud, if you wanna live in a village you've gotta be a villager sometimes."

In short, Forever's turned me into a big, fluffy, golden-haired dog. The kind you meet in a park that bounds up to you with its stupid tongue wagging out. All that oldschool game design and camaraderie has, as it turns out, been a complete antidote to my hermetic ways. And while my street cred as a tough, solemn badass might never recover, I'm glad to be taking my time.

Harvey's history with games started when he first begged his parents for a World of Warcraft subscription aged 12, though he's since been cursed with Final Fantasy 14-brain and a huge crush on G'raha Tia. He made his start as a freelancer, writing for websites like Techradar, The Escapist, Dicebreaker, The Gamer, Into the Spine—and of course, PC Gamer. He'll sink his teeth into anything that looks interesting, though he has a soft spot for RPGs, soulslikes, roguelikes, deckbuilders, MMOs, and weird indie titles. He also plays a shelf load of TTRPGs in his offline time. Don't ask him what his favourite system is, he has too many.
